title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure rather than a model failure. A person with legitimate credentials used law enforcement databases and camera systems for a purpose those systems were not built to serve, and the misuse was personal rather than operational. The systems performed as designed for an authorised user, which is precisely why nothing in the deployment stopped it.

The failure sits at the point of use, not at the point of build. Database and camera access is granted to officers because the job requires it, and the check on that access is the officer's own compliance with the terms of the job. Catching this kind of misuse requires auditing queries and camera lookups against case records, or flagging searches that have no investigative predicate attached. The reporting does not say whether any such audit existed.

What is established is an indictment on eight counts and a termination when the investigation began. The charges are allegations, and an indictment is not a conviction. Whether the systems logged the activity, whether anyone reviewed those logs, and what the court will find are not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors say he misused law enforcement databases and camera systems for personal reasons, including tracking and surveilling a woman without her consent between April and May 2024. He was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman, who spoke anonymously, said she waited two years for the investigation and hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
